slot.brief: Set up and compute the area bounded by a parabola/line pair or two curves with a simple intersection.

stem: Find the area enclosed by the parabola $y=4x-x^2$ and the line $y=2x$.

verdicts.working: Intersections: 4x − x² = 2x gives x = 0, 2. The area is ∫₀²(2x − x²) dx = 4/3.

working:
$4x-x^2=2x\Rightarrow x=0,2$.\n$\text{Area}=\displaystyle\int_0^2\big[(4x-x^2)-2x\big]dx=\left[x^2-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2=\dfrac{4}{3}$.

Independent check: Intersections: 4x − x² = 2x gives x = 0, 2. The area is ∫₀²(2x − x²) dx = 4/3.
solution:
The curves intersect where $4x-x^2=2x$, giving $x=0,2$. Between these points, the parabola lies above the line.
$$\text{Area}=\int_0^2\big[(4x-x^2)-2x\big]dx=\left[x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2=\frac{4}{3}\text{ square units}.$$
